metadata.title: RED VELVET CUPCAKE MILKSHAKE - The Scran Line
metadata.description:
These Red Velvet Cupcake Milkshake have an actual cupcake in them so you get your dose of Vitamin C. It's delicious, and makes the perfect summertime, weekend treat!

Loved the video? You'll find the recipe here:
http://www.thescranline.com/#!red-velvet-cupcake-milkshake/c9kp

Grab my Red Velvet recipe here:
http://www.thescranline.com/#!red-velvet-cupcake/c1j5p

Grab my Cream Cheese Frosting recipe here:
http://www.thescranline.com/#!easy-cream-cheese-frosting/c1jxr

Follow me on social media and keep up to date during the week!
- facebook.com/TheScranLine
- instagram.com/TheScranLine
- twitter.com/TheScranLine

nodes.plm_action: Assemble the ingredients and make the mixture.
nodes.plm_caption:
In the beginning of the video, a man standing in a kitchen is talking directly into the camera. He wears a striped shirt and an apron. Several pictures of cakes and a hand pointing to different ingredients are briefly shown.
In the middle of the video, more pictures of ingredients are shown, then a person takes the ingredients and makes a milkshake in a blender. While making the shake, some of the ingredients pour into the glass.
In the final moments, the man in the kitchen is talking to the camera and two more pictures of a cupcake and the same hand pointing to the ingredient are briefly shown.

summary.brief: Nick mixes a red‑velvet cupcake milkshake and serves it in a mason jar.
summary.detailed: Nick greets the viewer in a kitchen while animated “The Scran Line” graphics play, then points to a layout of ingredients that includes a red‑velvet cupcake, vanilla ice cream, milk, cocoa powder, red food dye, whipped cream and chocolate sauce. He whips the cream with a whisk, adds the milk, a scoop of ice cream, vanilla extract, cocoa powder, red dye and a piece of the cupcake to a blender, blends on high until smooth, and pours the shake into a clear mason jar. He drizzles chocolate sauce down the sides of the jar, tops it with a dollop of whipped cream, sprinkles red‑velvet crumbs, and inserts a red‑and‑white striped straw. The video ends with a close‑up of the finished shake beside a frosted cupcake and on‑screen overlays directing viewers to the recipe website and to subscribe.

action.detailed: Whip the cream, then combine milk, a scoop of vanilla ice cream, cocoa powder, red food dye and a piece of red‑velvet cupcake in a blender, blend on high until smooth, pour into a mason jar, drizzle chocolate sauce down the sides, top with whipped cream and red‑velvet crumbs, and insert a red‑and‑white striped straw.

nodes.plm_caption:
The video shows a woman's hands preparing a recipe to make red velvet ice cream in a mason jar. It begins with her introducing the recipe to the camera using her right hand while she touches the items on the table. Then it shows her showing a stick blender, ice cream, milk, two flavoring droppers, a red velvet cake, a vanilla and a Philadelphia cream cheese. Then it shows her putting some of the cream cheese into the blender with the milk and the red velvet cake. It shows a cup filled with vanilla ice cream. It then shows the blender being put on and it and the cup of vanilla ice cream being put into the blender.
It then shows the blender being set and the woman starting to mix. It shows the blender being taken out and the contents being transferred to the jar. Then it shows the jar being filled with the ice cream and the red velvet cake being poured on top. It then shows the mason jar being filled with whipped cream and red velvet cake.
The final shot shows the finished product.
The video is titled "theScranLine".

summary.brief: A hand blends red‑velvet ingredients, pours the shake into a mason jar, and tops it with chocolate sauce, whipped cream and cake crumbs.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with a close‑up of a white countertop covered with the recipe’s components—Philadelphia cream cheese, milk, pieces of red‑velvet cupcake, vanilla ice‑cream, cocoa powder, vanilla extract, chocolate sauce and colorful sprinkles. A hand points to each item, opens the cream‑cheese package and adds a portion to a bowl, then adds milk and the cupcake pieces. A scoop of vanilla ice‑cream is dropped in, and the mixture is briefly whisked. The contents are transferred to a clear stick‑blender, the blender is turned on at high speed and blended until the mixture is smooth and uniformly red. The thick shake is poured from the blender into a tall mason jar. Chocolate sauce is drizzled down the sides of the jar, a generous dollop of whipped cream is placed on top, and the surface is sprinkled with red‑velvet crumbs and extra sprinkles. Finally a striped straw is positioned in the jar and the completed red‑velvet milkshake is shown.

action.detailed: Add cream cheese, milk, cupcake pieces and ice‑cream to a bowl, whisk briefly, blend the mixture in a stick‑blender until smooth, pour the shake into a mason jar, drizzle chocolate sauce, top with whipped cream and red‑velvet crumbs, and insert a striped straw.

llm.system_prompt:
You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,
a hierarchical GPT-written summary of the whole video, and a deduplicated list
of action labels extracted at multiple levels of the video.

Your job is to judge:

1) DOMAINS — does this video clearly belong to either of these target domains?
   - "kitchen": a person preparing food in a kitchen-like setting
     (cooking, baking, food prep — NOT eating reviews, NOT pet-food prep,
     NOT food-product unboxing, NOT restaurant vlogs).
   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   A video can match neither, one, or both. Be strict — when in doubt,
   say "neither".

2) NUM_DISTINCT_EVENTS — count the number of *semantically distinct*
   sub-events (procedural steps) you see in the action list. Merge
   paraphrases of the same step into one. Ignore generic narration steps
   like "speak to camera" or "display title".

3) IS_GOOD_CANDIDATE — true only if BOTH:
   - at least one target domain matches
   - num_distinct_events > 3 (the video shows a real multi-step procedure)

Always return strict JSON in the requested schema.
